summary: U.S. startups continued to secure sizable rounds, led by brain-computer interface company Science securing a fresh $400 million.
title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: $400M For Neurotech Leads, Followed By Big Deals For AI, Fintech, Biotech And More

summary: What if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth? Or researchers could send an experiment into space for less than the price of a car? Our latest roundup also includes a company bringing AI to the old-school business of garbage hauling, another rethinking how factories are programmed, and a consumer brand betting that better breathing could become a big business.
title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Reflecting Sunlight From Space, Better Breathing And Smarter Garbage Trucks

summary: The AI buildout’s growing reliance on debt echoes the telecom bubble, raising the risk that infrastructure spending will outpace the revenue needed to meet fixed repayment obligations. According to guest author David Spreng of Runway Growth Capital, even if AI fulfills its technological promise, borrowers’ survival will depend on realistic demand forecasts and debt tied to dependable cash flows, with missed timelines potentially forcing restructurings and bankruptcies.
title: What The Telecom Bust Taught Me About AI’s Debt Boom

summary: The $2.6 trillion blue economy is creating startup opportunities in maritime automation, clean energy and logistics, with blue tech funding nearing $10 billion through Q3 2026, driven largely by major defense deals. Alberto Onetti, chairman of Mind the Bridge, writes that ports are emerging as hubs for testing and scaling these technologies, but realizing their potential requires coordination among port authorities, startups, investors and policymakers.
title: The Blue Economy: The World’s Quietest Economic Engine And Its Smartest Cities

summary: So far this year, venture backers have poured close to $4 billion into an assortment of global companies focused on recruiting, finding jobs and streamlining processes associated with HR and payroll management, Crunchbase data shows. Not surprisingly, the vast majority are also incorporating a heavy dose of AI.
title: What’s Next For Recruiting, Job Hunting And HR? More AI, Of Course

summary: The “SaaSpocalypse” selloff and uneven recovery exposed public markets’ difficulty distinguishing software companies that benefit from AI from those it threatens, particularly as deeply embedded platforms retain competitive advantages. In this guest essay, Richard Anton, co-founder and general partner of Oxx, argues that this volatility distorts private transaction pricing, undermines confidence in public ownership and makes IPOs less appealing to founders.
title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why

summary: The offering promises to be the public market event of the season, with the Claude creator seeing investor demand for shares well in excess of its capital-raising goals.
title: Anthropic Closes Up 17% After Massive IPO

summary: Just three years after launching with zero revenue, Anthropic brought in $17 billion and says more than 11,900 customers now spend at least $100,000 a year. But its IPO filing also reveals enormous computing commitments and big questions about balancing growth with risks.
title: The Key Numbers I’m Watching As Anthropic Makes Its IPO Debut

summary: AI companies’ hybrid subscription, usage and outcome-based pricing makes headline ARR figures an unreliable measure of predictable revenue, often obscuring differences in customer commitments and spending patterns. Guest author Kenza Zayani, an early-stage investor at RTP Global, warns that as these businesses seek growth capital, investors increasingly expect evidence of retention, expansion, revenue predictability and sustainable margins to assess the durability of growth.
title: What To Measure When ARR Isn’t Enough

summary: Voice AI is drawing billions of dollars from investors as startups find more ways to put it to work. According to Crunchbase data, companies developing or offering the technology have raised at least $9.5 billion in venture funding so far in 2026.
title: Sector Snapshot: Investors Turn Up The Volume On Voice AI
